cues.text: This continues the cabin from tutorial 2, so the units are set. Let's dress it up.
On the Materials tab, open the Material Manager.
Each material is now a little sphere wearing it, rendered with the real shaders.
The Model tab holds this model's materials. The Library tab holds ready-made ones.
Plain colors first, then vegetation, then construction: brick, tiles, stone, glass, metal.
Select the four walls.
Pick Red brick, then Apply to Selection. That adds it to the model and paints the walls.
Ooh, real bricks. The tick marks library materials already in the model.
Now a texture for the roof. Back on the Model tab, choose New Material.
Name it, then give it an image. Browse opens a file dialog; typing the path works too.
The image covers 4 by 4 units. That's 1.2 metres in this model.
Select the roof, then Apply to Selection.
Hmm, the boards are narrow. Choose Edit Texture Position, then click the roof.
Drag a corner to size the image. The opposite corner stays put.
Nice, wider boards. The drag is saved to the material, and Undo takes it back.
Next, something shiny on the lawn. Press T on the grid for a helper.
Sphere: pick a centre up the helper, then a point above it for the radius.
New Material now lists every shader in one place. Open the Program list.
Emboss tiling, rough stone, metal, glass and Perlin noise. Pick Polished metal.
The sphere is still selected, so Apply to Selection.
Look, a mirror. Metal reflects a studio sky with hard highlights.
Shader Programs lists every program and what uses it.
Deleting a custom program turns its materials back into plain ones.
New Shader opens the shader editor. Full Source shows exactly what gets compiled.
No hidden layers. We won't write one today, so Cancel.
Last, the lawn. Rectangle, and click two grid points around the cabin.
In the Library, double-click Grass. It joins the model with a tick.
Then Apply to Selection.
Wooow. Every material is saved with the project, and stays editable.
And the Model tab now shows them all: brick, decking, metal and grass.
